arxiv-2009-02091.title: A canonical tree-of-tangles theorem for structurally submodular separation systems
arxiv-2009-02091.creator: Christian Elbracht, Jakob Kneip
arxiv-2009-02091.description: Abstract We show that every structurally submodular separation system admits a canonical tree set which distinguishes its tangles. 1 Introduction The concept of tangles has its origins in the graph minors project of Robertson and Seymour [ 6 ] , where tangles were introduced as a unifying framework with which to describe and study highly cohesive substructures in graphs.

arxiv-2106-09917.title: Envy-freeness and Relaxed Stability for Lower-Quotas : A Parameterized Perspective
arxiv-2106-09917.creator: Girija Limaye
arxiv-2106-09917.description: Abstract We consider the problem of assigning agents to resources under the two-sided preference list model where resources specify an upper-quota and a lower-quota, that is, respectively the maximum and minimum number of agents that can be assigned to it.

arxiv-2212-08613.title: Atrous Space Bender U-Net (ASBU-Net/LogiNet)
arxiv-2212-08613.creator: Anurag Bansal Oleg Ostap Miguel Maestre Trueba Kristopher Perry
arxiv-2212-08613.description: Abstract With recent advances in CNNs, exceptional improvements have been made in semantic segmentation of high resolution image in terms of accuracy and latency. However, challenges still remain in detecting objects in crowded scenes, large scale variations, partial occlusion, and distortions, while still maintaining mobility and latency.

arxiv-2301-09282.title: Classification of Luminal Subtypes in Full Mammogram Images Using Transfer Learning
arxiv-2301-09282.creator: Adarsh Bhandary Panambur, Prathmesh Madhu, Andreas Maier
arxiv-2301-09282.description: Abstract Automatic identification of patients with luminal and non-luminal subtypes during a routine mammography screening can support clinicians in streamlining breast cancer therapy planning. Recent machine learning techniques have shown promising results in molecular subtype classification in mammography; however, they are highly dependent on pixel-level annotations, handcrafted, and radiomic features.

arxiv-2307-15061.title: The Robo Depth Challenge: Methods and Advancements Towards Robust Depth Estimation
arxiv-2307-15061.creator: Lingdong Kong, Yaru Niu, Shaoyuan Xie, Hanjiang Hu, Lai Xing Ng, Benoit R. Cottereau, Liangjun Zhang, Hesheng Wang, Wei Tsang Ooi, Ruijie Zhu, Ziyang Song, Li Liu, Tianzhu Zhang, Jun Yu, Mohan Jing, Pengwei Li, Xiaohua Qi, Cheng Jin, Yingfeng Chen, Jie Hou, Jie Zhang, Zhen Kan, Qiang Ling, Liang Pen
arxiv-2307-15061.description: Abstract Accurate depth estimation under out-of-distribution (OoD) scenarios, such as adverse weather conditions, sensor failure, and noise contamination, is desirable for safety-critical applications. Existing depth estimation systems, however, suffer inevitably from real-world corruptions and perturbations and are struggled to provide reliable depth predictions under such cases.

arxiv-2312-15580.title: Magneto-chiral backscatterings by rotationally symmetric nonreciprocal structures
arxiv-2312-15580.creator: Chunchao Wen, Jianfa Zhang, Shiqiao Qin, Zhihong Zhu, Wei Liu
arxiv-2312-15580.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Chunchao Wen, Jianfa Zhang, Shiqiao Qin, Zhihong Zhu, Wei Liu. It was proved that the joint operation of electromagnetic reciprocity and n n -fold ( n ≥ 3 n\geq 3 ) rotational symmetry would secure arbitrary polarization-independent backscattering efficiency [Phys. B 103 , 045422 (2021)]. Here we remove the restriction of reciprocity and study the backscatterings of plane waves by rotationally symmetric magneto-optical structures, with collinear incident wavevector, rotational axis and externally applied magnetic field.

arxiv-2401-17268.title: Weaver : Foundation Models for Creative Writing
arxiv-2401-17268.creator: Tiannan Wang Jiamin Chen Qingrui Jia Shuai Wang Ruoyu Fang Huilin Wang Zhaowei Gao Chunzhao Xie Chuou Xu Jihong Dai Yibin Liu Jialong Wu Shengwei Ding Long Li Zhiwei Huang Xinle Deng Teng Yu Gangan Ma Han Xiao Zixin Chen Danjun Xiang Yunxia Wang Yuanyuan Zhu Yi Xiao Jing Wang Yiru Wang Siran Ding Ji
arxiv-2401-17268.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Tiannan Wang Jiamin Chen Qingrui Jia Shuai Wang Ruoyu Fang Huilin Wang Zhaowei Gao Chunzhao Xie Chuou Xu Jihong Dai Yibin Liu Jialong Wu Shengwei Ding Long Li Zhiwei Huang Xinle Deng Teng Yu Gangan Ma Han Xiao Zixin Chen Danjun Xiang Yunxia Wang Yuanyuan Zhu Yi Xiao Jing Wang Yiru Wang Siran Ding Ji. This work introduces Weaver , our first family of large language models (LLMs) dedicated to content creation.

arxiv-2410-20369.title: Langevin deformation for Rényi entropy on Wasserstein space over Riemannian manifolds
arxiv-2410-20369.creator: Rong Lei, Songzi Li, Xiang-Dong Li
arxiv-2410-20369.description: Abstract We introduce the Langevin deformation for the Rényi entropy on the L 2 L^{2} -Wasserstein space over ℝ n \mathbb{R}^{n} or a Riemannian manifold, which interpolates between the porous medium equation and the Benamou-Brenier geodesic flow on the L 2 L^{2} -Wasserstein space and can be regarded as the compressible Euler equations for isentropic gas with damping.

arxiv-2510-09615.title: A Biosecurity Agent for Lifecycle LLM Biosecurity Alignment
arxiv-2510-09615.creator: Meiyin Meng, Zaixi Zhang
arxiv-2510-09615.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Meiyin Meng, Zaixi Zhang. Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly integrated into biomedical research workflows—from literature triage and hypothesis generation to experimental design—yet this expanded utility also heightens dual-use concerns, including the potential misuse for guiding toxic compound synthesis. In response, this study shows a Biosecurity Agent that comprises four coordinated modes across the model lifecycle: dataset sanitization, preference alignment, runtime guardrails, and automated red teaming.

arxiv-2601-10740.title: Neuro-Symbolic Activation Discovery: Transferring Mathematical Structures from Physics to Ecology for Parameter-Efficient Neural Networks
arxiv-2601-10740.creator: Anas Hajbi
arxiv-2601-10740.description: Abstract Modern neural networks rely on generic activation functions (ReLU, GELU, SiLU) that ignore the mathematical structure inherent in scientific data. We propose Neuro-Symbolic Activation Discovery , a framework that uses Genetic Programming to extract interpretable mathematical formulas from data and inject them as custom activation functions.

arxiv-2601-20527.title: Thermodynamic Consistency as a Reliability Test for Complex Langevin Simulations
arxiv-2601-20527.creator: Arpith Kumar
arxiv-2601-20527.description: Abstract The complex Langevin method (CLM) is a promising tool to address the sign problem in quantum field theories with complex actions. However, it can converge to incorrect results even when simulations appear stable, highlighting the need for robust diagnostics. Existing checks, such as monitoring drift distributions, are useful but indirect.

europmc-pmc9499024.description: Bacterial mobile genetic elements (MGEs) encode functional modules that perform both core and accessory functions for the element, the latter of which are often only transiently associated with the element. pmc-10531914.title: Chronic Vestibular Hypofunction Is Associated with Impaired Sleep: Results from the DizzyReg Patient Registry
pmc-10531914.creator: Benedict Katzenberger, Fiona Brosch, Stéphane Besnard, Eva Grill
pmc-10531914.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Temporary or permanent vestibular hypofunction has been hypothesized to affect circadian rhythm, sleep, and thermoregulation. Chronic or long-term vestibular disorders such as unilateral vestibular hypofunction may have an even greater negative impact on sleep quality than acute vestibular problems. This study examines self-reported sleep quality, as assessed by the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), and its association with vestibular symptom duration in a group of patients with vestibular disorders.

pmc-10732917.creator: Computational Intelligence and Neuroscience

pmc-11363712.title: Associations of five dietary indices with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease and liver fibrosis among the United States population
pmc-11363712.creator: Min Xu, Yamei Zhan, Guohui Gao, Li Zhu, Tong Wu, Guijie Xin
pmc-11363712.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Background and aimsThe role of dietary factors in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD)—which represents a new definition of liver steatosis and metabolic dysfunction— remains unclear. This study aimed to explore the relationships between dietary indices and MASLD.MethodsWe analyzed data from the United States National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 2017–2020 cycle, including 4,690 participants with complete vibration-controlled transient elastography (VCTE) data.

pmc-12515583.title: U2AF2 Missense Variant Associated With Epilepsy and Systemic Dysmorphism: Report of Two Cases and Literature Review
pmc-12515583.creator: Shiqin Huang, Mei Li, Hai Yuan, Yunli Han, Xiaolan Chen, Yunxuan Su, Xing Li
pmc-12515583.description: Recurrent U2AF2 c.445C>T variant in two cases with systemic dysmorphism, epilepsy, and neurodevelopmental regression suggests a novel spliceosomal gene‐brain disorder link, warranting U2AF2 screening in unexplained neurodevelopmental cases. Introduction U2 auxiliary factor (U2AF) is a non‐snRNP protein that is crucial for the binding of U2 snRNP to the pre‐mRNA branch site.

pmc-12589241.title: Patient:innen profitieren von Informationen
pmc-12589241.creator: Markus Schneider
pmc-12589241.description: HintergrundBei Betrachtung der Schmerzursachen kam es in den letzten 20–30 Jahren zu einem erheblichen Paradigmenwechsel. Während historisch gesehen die biomedizinische Betrachtungsweise eines direkten Zusammenhanges zwischen Gewebeschaden und Schmerzstärke im Vordergrund stand, zeigt sich zunehmend, das Schmerzempfinden ein hoch komplexes System ist, dass biologische, psychische und soziale Faktoren einschließt und dem früheren Verständnis entgegensteht.

pmc-12659313.title: Post-valvular energy exchange in bicuspid aortic valve with regurgitation and stenosis and its association with left ventricular workload: a 4D flow magnetic resonance imaging cross-sectional study
pmc-12659313.creator: Shirin Aliabadi, Dina Labib, Sandra Rivest, James A. White, Julio Garcia
pmc-12659313.description: BackgroundBicuspid aortic valve (BAV) regurgitation and stenosis considerably alter post-valvular flow dynamics and impose additional energetic load on the left ventricle (LV). We therefore sought to determine whether 4D Flow MRI-derived ascending-aortic kinetic energy (KE) and viscous energy loss (EL), can differentiate BAV subtypes and healthy controls, and are associated with LV remodeling markers.

pmc-12704266.title: β-Hydroxybutyrate ameliorates lipopolysaccharide-induced liver injury through β-hydroxybutyrylation of the SOD2 protein in mice
pmc-12704266.creator: Ya-Ping Bai, Yan Zhang, Zhi-Yuan Chen, Kai Li, De-Guo Wang, Shu-Jun Wan, Cui-Wei Zhang, Yue Sun, Zhi-Chao Li, Kun Lv, Lei Zha, Xiang Kong
pmc-12704266.description: Septic liver injury is a major complication of sepsis, driven in part by oxidative stress–induced macrophage inflammasome activation and hepatocyte apoptosis. β-Hydroxybutyrate (β-OHB), a key ketone body, induces lysine β-hydroxybutyrylation (Kbhb), a novel post-translational modification, yet its role in septic liver injury remains unclear.

pmc-13083270.title: An illustrated guide to dissection and abdominal anatomy of the yellow mealworm beetle
pmc-13083270.creator: Chloé Rosa-Teijeiro, Fanny Renois, Marie-Odile Benoit-Biancamano
pmc-13083270.description: An unprecedented increase in the number and the size of yellow mealworm beetle (Tenebrio molitor) farms in North America and Europe has been driven, among other factors, by the demand for sustainable proteins. Insect farming offers ecologic advantages, including lower land and water use and reduced greenhouse gas emissions.

pmc-13335344.title: Computer modeling to improve measurement of stroke volume with echocardiography
pmc-13335344.creator: Sarah Balderston Murthi, Shiming Yang, Peter P Oliveri, Sami Safadi, Sydea Fatima, William Teeter
pmc-13335344.description: BackgroundThe stroke volume (SV) can be measured by a human expert (HE) using the left ventricular outflow tract diameter (LVOTd) and its velocity time integral (VTI) with echo. If the SV is known, the cardiac output and systemic vascular resistance can be calculated. We have previously described a machine learning computer model (CM) to estimate the LVOTd.

pmc-13475514.title: Reply to: “Interpreting infection–disease associations in psoriasis and atopic dermatitis”
pmc-13475514.creator: Zhiru Zhou, Yi Xiao
pmc-13475514.description: n opportunity to further clarify the interpretation of our findings. Regarding temporality, we acknowledge that reverse causation is a recognized limitation in observational research. Importantly, our meta-analysis was restricted to cohort studies in which infection exposure preceded disease diagnosis, which represents a methodological strength over cross-sectional designs.

pmc-13485250.title: The Stabilization of High‐Nitrogen Systems: 10 Catenated Nitrogen Chain
pmc-13485250.creator: Nicholas F Scherschel, Thomas R Talbot, Matthias Zeller, Davin G Piercey
pmc-13485250.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). High‐nitrogen materials have attracted intense interest in recent decades due to their unique chemical, physical, and biological properties. Stabilizing high‐nitrogen materials is often challenging as they become more unstable with increasing nitrogen catenation and nitrogen mass percentage increase. Although approaches such as introducing alternating positive/negative charges and restricting electrocyclic N2 loss have been reported for stabilizing high‐nitrogen systems, these structural motifs have not previously been applied to highly catenated nitrogen chains.

pmc-13628965.title: Operationalizing transparency regarding the use of health data for research: a cross-sectional survey of citizens’ perspectives
pmc-13628965.creator: Annabelle Cumyn, Jean-Frédéric Ménard, Emmanuel Bilodeau, Roxanne Dault, Jean-Philippe Morissette, Marie-Pier Domingue, Félix Camirand Lemyre, Denis Boutin, Jean-François Ethier
pmc-13628965.description: BackgroundSecondary use of health data can accelerate discovery and enable personalized care, yet social acceptability relies on autonomy, transparency, and trust, especially in the context of security breaches and concerns about misuse. In Quebec, as in many Western settings, there is no formal mechanism to inform individuals about such use, underscoring the need for practical solutions.
